The passmcp family

Nine components, one version.

The family moves in lockstep: one version across every component, released together. Each status links to its release, or to the changelog that tracks what is not released yet.

The components of the passmcp family, what each is for, and its release status
ComponentPurposeStatus
passmcpThe engine, every check, and the three peer surfaces: CLI, TUI and the embedded local web UI.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-reportingThe attestation predicate, its JSON Schema and the offline verifier, as a module with no dependencies; the report schema, the renderers and the rubric as data follow when a consumer needs them.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-serverAn MCP server exposing passmcp's diagnostics as read-only tools, so an agent can evaluate a server, or check an attestation about one, from inside the editor.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-actionThe GitHub Action wrapping the published image by digest, and a GitLab CI template.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-graphA local graph of which agents use which MCP servers, which tools those servers expose and which identities reach them, built from passmcp's attestations, reports and MCP client configurations, queried offline and gated by policy in CI.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-registryA signed public scorecard of the remote servers in the MCP Registry: each checked read-only and without credentials by a pinned passmcp release, every result an offline-verifiable attestation, and anything that would expose a vulnerability withheld for its owner first.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-lspA language server over MCP artefacts — server.json, tool schemas, client configuration, passmcp policy and attestation files — with check-id hover from the guidance catalogue.Released in 0.0.3
passmcp-censusThe published reliability census: the dataset, the methodology, the disclosure log and the reproduction command.Released in 0.0.3
satellion.comThe public site at satellion.com, built with SSG against passmcp's latest release: the home page, the manual and a sample report passmcp generates.Released in 0.0.3

Considered and rejected

Components proposed for the family and decided against, with the reason.

Components considered for the passmcp family and rejected, with the reason
ComponentPurposeWhy not
passmcp-gatewayAn in-path MCP gateway.Fourteen incumbents, two of them free and open source, one of them AWS. Being in the data path would also convert passmcp from a tool that touches nothing into a production dependency trusted with traffic.
passmcp-wasmA browser build of the engine.CORS blocks a browser build against most servers. A build target, not a repository.
passmcp-proxyAn in-path proxy that inspects, or sanitises and rewrites, live traffic between an agent and a server (also proposed as passmcp-inspector and passmcp-shield).The gateway again under another name: in the data path is in the data path whether it only watches or also rewrites (ADR 0007). A rewriting shield would also judge by classifier rather than cite the request that showed the property (ADR 0002). Live inspection is the official MCP Inspector's job.
passmcp-fuzzA stress and fuzzing tool that sends servers malformed input, oversized payloads and connection churn (also proposed as passmcp-chaos).An adversarial mode in its own repository, which ADR 0008 rules out behind a flag and behind a verb alike: the read-only posture is what lets a security team approve passmcp. Resilience is already a phase of the check, and passmcp fuzzes its own parsers.
